transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Scheduled duration: 60m (ran ~62m)
Attendees: Ethan Moore (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (BlueHarbor Platform Lead), Marco Ruiz (BlueHarbor SRE), Tobias Meyer (BlueHarbor Security), Dana Lee (BlueHarbor PM)
Links referenced: deck - https://redwood.ai/links/blueharbor-integration, benchmark sheet - https://sheets.redwood.ai/blueharbor-bench, runbook draft - https://docs.blueharbor.com/runbooks/rdw-interop

Summary (auto):
Quick technical deep dive to align on hybrid deployment orchestration patterns, rollback/canary strategy, telemetry requirements for marketplace listing, and KMS/pass-through expectations for Private mode. Agreed next steps for benchmarks and pricing followup.

Transcript (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Ethan Moore: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan with Redwood, AE. We have Lucas and Maya from the SE team. How's everyone doing at BlueHarbor?
[00:16] Aisha Khan: Hey Ethan, yeah doing good. Busy week but excited to get into the orchestration details. We're mostly focused on how Redwood fits into our hybrid stack and the rollback story.
[00:30] Lucas Chen: Hi all, Lucas here. We'll try to make this practical: show the recommended patterns for canary/rollback, what we need for KMS, and a quick sketch of telemetry hooks you can expect.
[00:45] Marco Ruiz: Quick note from SRE side: our biggest concerns are spike handling during peak and a straightforward rollback that doesn't leave stale routes. Also, operator friendliness — helm charts, quick-run playbook.
[01:05] Maya Patel: Totally. We'll walk through dedicated pools, autoscale boundaries, and the model variant fallback so you can degrade gracefully cost-wise.
[01:18] Dana Lee: And from product, I'm trying to understand the UX differences users will see during a canary vs full rollout — latency differences, error modes.
[01:34] Ethan Moore: Great framing. Agenda: (1) deployment topologies (hosted/dedicated/private hybrid), (2) canary/rollback orchestration, (3) telemetry and audit logs for marketplace listing, (4) KMS and network constraints, (5) benchmarks and next steps.
[01:50] Lucas Chen: On topologies: the common pattern we recommend for hybrid is control plane hosted, data plane in your VPC for Private; for Dedicated it's a reserved pool that can be pinned to a region. For a hybrid deployment your ingress typically lives in BlueHarbor, and the RDW agents in your VPC handle inference calls. This keeps egress and data residency aligned.
[02:22] Marco Ruiz: When you say "RDW agents" can you clarify — is that a containerized runtime we run?
[02:30] Lucas Chen: Yes, it's a helm-packaged runtime. Think of it as an inference gateway + runtime. We ship a helm chart with values for quant profiles, kernel selection hints, and KV cache sizing. It's not heavy; runs on 2-4 GPU nodes depending on model.
[02:50] Aisha Khan: Do we need to maintain model artifacts on our side? We prefer Redwood to host model binaries where possible.
[02:58] Maya Patel: We support both. For Private/on-prem you can host the model in your cluster (air-gapped option) or pull a vendor-verified quantized image from Redwood's registry with explicit hashes. For compliance you can pin the model and verify checksums.
[03:20] Tobias Meyer: About KMS: BlueHarbor uses Vault HSM-backed KMS. How do you integrate? We can't have plaintext keys leaving our VPC.
[03:34] Lucas Chen: We support KMS passthrough and HSM integrations. For Private we can configure the runtime to use your KMS endpoint — no keys leave the VPC. We'll need a TLS-mTLS setup and a short-lived token exchange during startup, we document that in the runbook.
[03:54] Ethan Moore: I'll attach the KMS integration playbook after the call.
[04:00] Marco Ruiz: Cool. Next, rollback. What's your recommended safe rollback procedure? We need a stage where traffic is split and can be taken back without losing session state.
[04:15] Lucas Chen: Good question. Pattern A: traffic-split canary (10% traffic) using smart routing with sticky session TTL on the KV cache to maintain cache locality. If p50/p95 is good, increase. If degradation observed, automatic fallback rules re-route to previous variant. Pattern B: blue/green where you warm caches in green, then switch ingress. Blue/green is better for larger model weights to avoid cache cold-starts.
[04:50] Dana Lee: That sticky session TTL — does that require changes to our API gateway?
[04:56] Lucas Chen: Ideally yes: a cookie or header-based sticky routing. We also have an edge router option that can do weighted routing and header-based steering if you don't want gateway changes.
[05:12] Aisha Khan: For marketplace listing, we need reproducible telemetry: audit logs, token-level cost estimates, and traceability. What telemetry do you emit out-of-the-box?
[05:28] Maya Patel: Out-of-the-box: request traces (trace id), token counts, model_id, variant, latency buckets, error codes. We can also emit Prometheus metrics and a dedicated telemetry endpoint to ship to your observability stack. Audit logs for request metadata can be delivered to S3 or to your SIEM.
[05:50] Tobias Meyer: Does audit include the prompt body? We have to be careful with PII.
[05:55] Lucas Chen: We avoid storing prompt plaintext by default. Audit logs include hashes/pseudonymized IDs and metadata. If you enable debug capture, it requires explicit consent and secure storage.
[06:15] Marcus Ruiz (sic) [note: speaker name sometimes transcribed wrong]: Sorry that's Marco. One more on telemetry: do you provide alerting thresholds or do we wire up our own?
[06:24] Maya Patel: We provide default alert templates (p90 latency breach, cache hit ratio drop, error rate spike) you can plug into your pager.
[06:34] Ethan Moore: I want to highlight the fallback model variant option: for cost/latency tradeoff you can route to a quantized smaller variant when latency spikes. That gives graceful degradation rather than full outage.
[06:50] Aisha Khan: Ok that sounds promising. How do you manage model variant compatibility? Are there compatibility guarantees between the full and quant model?
[06:58] Lucas Chen: We maintain an artifact compatibility matrix. For quantized variants we publish a quality delta and a canonical prompt set so you can see regressions. For marketplace listing, we require a documented quality budget if you intend to fallback to a lower-quality variant.
[07:20] Dana Lee: We'll need that canonical prompt set for our acceptance tests.
[07:27] Lucas Chen: We'll share a suggested prompt suite; you can add your domain-specific prompts.
[07:34] Marco Ruiz: Back to orchestration: what about autoscaling? If we have burst traffic, will scaling be fast enough to avoid p99 spikes?
[07:42] Maya Patel: Autoscaling for Dedicated pools is based on queue depth and token throughput. For Private, node-level autoscaling triggers can be mapped to your cluster autoscaler. For very spiky loads, we recommend a small burst capacity in Redwood Dedicated or pre-warm capacity — that avoids cold-starts.
[08:02] Tobias Meyer: Is the pre-warm approach compatible with our tenancy model? We want isolation for some routes.
[08:08] Lucas Chen: Yes, you can pin models/routes to isolated pools. That way pre-warm nodes are reserved for your critical routes.
[08:16] Ethan Moore: Quick callout on security reviews: for marketplace listing you'll need SOC2 artifacts, penetration test summary, and an encryption architecture diagram. We have an enterprise pack with those docs.
[08:30] Tobias Meyer: Good. Can you attach the penetration test summary?
[08:33] Ethan Moore: I'll attach the redacted pentest and SOC2 scope after the call.
[08:39] Aisha Khan: Next — deployment automation. We want the helm values we need to change for canary and rollback. Is there a sample values.yaml?
[08:48] Lucas Chen: Yes, we have a sample values.yaml showing canary weights, cache TTLs, quant profile toggles, and KMS config. It's in the runbook link. We'll send that link into the notes.
[09:02] Marco Ruiz: Can you walk through a failure scenario? Suppose the canary increases to 30% and p99 spikes then crash + OOM. What happens to in-flight sessions?
[09:14] Maya Patel: Two levels: (1) routing fallback to previous variant — traffic routed back; (2) we replay or rehydrate important session state if you have prefix caching. For long-running sessions we advise session checkpointing in your app layer. The runtime will try to keep KV cache warm but if nodes crash you'll face cold-start.
[09:36] Dana Lee: About session checkpointing — do you provide helpers or is that on BlueHarbor's app layer?
[09:43] Lucas Chen: Helpers: small SDK snippets for token-prefix reassembly, but most customers implement domain session checkpointing in their app service.
[09:52] Ethan Moore: Switching gears: marketplace listing checklist — we require a minimal telemetry contract, security docs, an integration test pass, and a packaging artifact (helm + manifest). BlueHarbor will need to fill the marketplace metadata template.
[10:10] Aisha Khan: Is there a standard manifest format?
[10:14] Maya Patel: Yes, YAML manifest with fields for images, hashes, supported regions, latency targets, required k8s CRDs. We'll share the manifest template.
[10:25] Marco Ruiz: On the helm chart — we want an operator mode that reconciles desired model versions. Is that supported?
[10:31] Lucas Chen: We have a lightweight operator that watches model CRs and triggers rollout flows. It also records status conditions that can be used in your dashboard.
[10:44] Tobias Meyer: A few quick compliance Qs: do you support customer-managed logs retention and can you disable retention in hosted mode?
[10:52] Maya Patel: For hosted mode we retain logs per agreement; for Private you control retention. We support pushing logs to your S3/GCS buckets with lifecycle rules you control.
[11:05] Ethan Moore: We should talk about concrete benchmarks. Lucas, can you outline what you'd need to run the 48-hour benchmark?
[11:12] Lucas Chen: We'll need a representative prompt set, traffic profile (qps, bursts), target models, and whether KV cache should be simulated. Preferably a dataset of 500-1000 prompts with length distribution. We'll run p50/p90/p95/p99, throughput, cost-per-token estimate, and cache-hit curves.
[11:34] Aisha Khan: We can share a sample prompt set but will scrub PII. We'll also include a short note on which endpoints are most critical.
[11:45] Lucas Chen: Great. We'll run the benchmark in your VPC Private runtime for the most realistic network profile. If you prefer Dedicated we can run against a reserved pool.
[11:58] Marco Ruiz: Any recommended quant profiles for our use-case (real-time chat + long form summarization)?
[12:06] Maya Patel: For low latency chat, 4-bit quant with KV cache on is effective. For long-form summarization prefer 8-bit to reduce quality drift. We'll provide an evaluation report showing rouge-like metrics over your prompt set.
[12:26] Dana Lee: That evaluation report will be super helpful for Product to decide fallback thresholds.
[12:33] Ethan Moore: I'll make sure we include quality deltas in the benchmark sheet.
[12:40] Aisha Khan: One more network question: we have strict egress rules to only a handful of IPs and a proxy. Can Redwood runtime operate behind a proxy?
[12:49] Lucas Chen: Yes. Our runtime supports proxy configuration and we can publish the IP ranges. For Private you can also keep everything internal and we don't require outbound except for optional telemetry endpoints.
[13:05] Tobias Meyer: If telemetry is optional, we want a pull model to fetch metrics on schedule rather than push.
[13:12] Maya Patel: We support both push and pull. Pulling from a metrics endpoint with mTLS is fine.
[13:20] Marco Ruiz: Great. Let's discuss a rough timeline for pilot: we'd like to run bench next week, then a 2-week pilot with Dedicated burst capacity, then a go/no-go for marketplace listing end of Oct. Feasible?
[13:34] Ethan Moore: Yes. Proposed: benchmarks run 10/6-10/8, pilot 10/12-10/26, listing readiness review week of 10/26. I'll confirm dates in writing.
[13:47] Aisha Khan: Sounds good.
[13:50] Dana Lee: On billing for the pilot — will my account be invoiced or is there a credit?
[13:57] Ethan Moore: Typical is either trial credits or a short-term reserved commitment. I'll send options.
[14:03] Lucas Chen: A small technical aside — the runtime has a KV cache snapshot/restore mechanism to speed up blue/green warms. It uses incremental checkpoints to S3-compatible storage. That helps reduce warm time dramatically.
[14:19] Marco Ruiz: Nice — what's typical warm time for a 64k contextual model?
[14:25] Lucas Chen: With checkpoints warmed to local SSDs you can get to 80% cache-warm in under 90s on a 4-GPU node; without it's several minutes. Exact numbers in the benchmark.
[14:40] Tobias Meyer: Anything else for security? We may ask for code-level review of the operator — is that allowed?
[14:47] Ethan Moore: We can offer a limited SOC2-scoped code review or redacted snippets; full source review requires an enterprise agreement. We'll escalate as needed.
[14:58] Aisha Khan: For marketplace listing, do you require a signed MSA first?
[15:04] Ethan Moore: Not strictly; we can do listing readiness and sandbox testing prior to an MSA, but production Dedicated will need a contract.
[15:13] Marco Ruiz: Can you also send a sample runbook for incident response for model regressions?
[15:19] Maya Patel: Yep, runbook draft link will be shared: includes rollback triggers, who to page, and playbook for KV cache rehydration.
[15:30] Lucas Chen: Small note on routing policies: you can route by latency SLO, cost bucket, or workspace; the runtime exposes a policy engine with weighted rules.
[15:41] Dana Lee: For canary metrics we'll need to see both latency and quality signals. Are quality signals available in near real-time?
[15:48] Lucas Chen: We can compute simple quality heuristics (e.g., BLEU/Rouge-ish approximations) in near real-time for known prompt types, but deep evals are offline. For near realtime we recommend a smaller set of signal prompts.
[16:04] Aisha Khan: Okay, let's capture action items and agree next steps.
[16:10] Ethan Moore: Recap: Lucas runs 48h benchmark in your environment w/ provided prompt set; Ethan sends pricing and SOC2/pentest redacted artifacts; BlueHarbor shares SLO doc and KMS vendor; schedule rollback demo 10/12.
[16:25] Marco Ruiz: That's accurate. Anything else?
[16:29] Tobias Meyer: Please include the manifest template and operator docs in the follow up.
[16:33] Maya Patel: We'll include sample values.yaml and operator CR examples.
[16:38] Aisha Khan: Thanks everyone. We'll look at dates and get the prompt set over by EOD tomorrow.
[16:46] Ethan Moore: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the attachments.
[16:50] Dana Lee: Bye.

End of transcript.
Notes: occasional speaker name mis-transcriptions observed (Marcus/Marco). Some technical terms transcribed as K V cache or k-want-ization in live auto-transcript; correct forms documented in attached runbook and deck.
